children: An analysis of insurance claims data found that if GLP-1 medications for weight loss and diabetes are priced below $350, it results in net savings for payors, such as employers and plan sponsors, through reduced use of health care services that result.
conducted the analysis based on claims from its health insurance unit, Aetna, of patients who recently started taking the drugs. Eli Lilly
markets Zepbound (tirzepatide) and Mounjaro (tirzepatide) for, respectively, obesity and type 2 diabetes, while Novo
Employers and health plan sponsors pay between $617 and $766 monthly for the GLP-1s, according to an October 2025 report by the Employee Benefit Research ​Institute.

At that level, the cost of the drugs wouldn't outweigh the savings from using fewer health care services. Lilly and Novo do offer their GLP-1s for self-pay customers ranging from $299 to $499 a month depending on dosage.
CVS Health Chief Medical Officer Amy Compton-Phillips told Reuters that she believes drugmakers could still turn a profit charging under $350 a month.
The analysis will be presented at the HLTH USA conference in Las Vegas on Sunday.

title: GLP-1s can save health system money if priced below $350 a month: analysis
